Release change (2026-10-10): Docker 29 removes an exited or stopped --rm container asynchronously: for several seconds `docker inspect` still shows it and `docker rm -f` answers "removal of container ... is already in progress" (exit 1); Docker 24 has removed it by then. agentloop/evaluator/product_lifecycle.py cleanup_owned (the exited --rm product container) and harbor/formal_one_stop.py cleanup_owned_container / cleanup_run_mounted_containers record rm's stderr and, when rm answers "already in progress", wait up to 30 s (inside the case's 90 s cleanup reserve for the product) for inspect to stop finding the container before deciding absent_after_cleanup. classify_incomplete: an unfrozen run whose last submission outcome is submission_not_consumed / public_or_launcher_infrastructure_failure is classified public_or_launcher_infrastructure_failure instead of latest_candidate_freeze_gate_failure. Any other rm refusal is judged as before, and a container still present after the wait is not absent. Seen with Docker 29.2.1.
